In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of fusion of C. tr.achomatis inclusions.
the fusion of chlamydia inclusions with each and with each other and the factors that control this fusion.
the fusion of C. tractomatis-containing inclusions with other intracellular compartments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fusion of C. tracomatis-containing inclusions with one another is an active process that requires protein synthesis by the bacteria.
the fusion of the C. trachomatis inclusion with other inclusions requires the production of a chlamydial protein(s) that is synthesized after the bacteria are inside the inclusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

C. trachomatisspecific inclusion fusion is inhibited at 32°C by a temperature-sensitive bacterial factor(s) that is secreted from the inclusion and requires bacterial protein synthesis for its activity.

fusion of inlusions with each other in C. trachamatis-infected cells occurs after the bacteria are released into the host cell cytosol, requires protein synthesis, and is not required for the production of infectious progeny.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fusion of inclusions is not a passive event, and the process is regulated in time and space.
C. trachmatis inclusion fusion requires a bacterial protein(s) and occurs only when the bacteria are replicating.
the fusion of C. tr.achomatis inclusions is a regulated process that occurs at the late developmental stage of the bacteria and that the regulation is mediated by a bacterial protein.
